screening_reasoning: Proposes TIB AIssistant, a domain-agnostic human-machine collaborative platform with modular components (prompt/tool libraries, shared data store, orchestration framework) for literature analysis and research workflow support. Explicitly describes system architecture and prototype implementation. Matches all inclusion criteria: computational tool for literature workflow (INC-01), incorporates LLMs/agentic orchestration (INC-02), describes provenance/audit mechanisms (INC-03), provides architecture specification (INC-04). No exclusion criteria apply.

Describes meta-pipe, a 10-stage open-source LLM-agent pipeline for end-to-end systematic review and meta-analysis with mandatory human oversight. Integrates Claude for screening/extraction, Python for automation, R for statistics, Quarto for rendering. Includes overclaim detection (12 patterns), semi-automated GRADE assessment, dual-paradigm NMA. Provides architecture, codebase (~3,600 lines), and empirical comparison with 5 existing tools. Matches all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply.

Presents QBD-RankedDataGen for generating custom ranked datasets to improve Query-By-Document search using LLM reranking. While it mentions academic literature review as one application domain, the primary focus is general-purpose IR dataset generation for patent matching, legal/compliance retrieval, not a scholarly literature workflow orchestration tool. Violates EXC-02 (general-purpose RAG/search not specifically targeted to academic research). Only weakly matches INC-02 (uses LLMs).

Empirical study evaluating citation hallucination rates across 4 LLMs and 5 prompting regimes with deterministic verification pipeline (Crossref + Semantic Scholar). While it evaluates citation verification (INC-03) and provides quantitative benchmarks (INC-04), it does not propose or implement a computational tool/harness for literature discovery, screening, extraction, or synthesis (fails INC-01). It is an evaluation study of LLM behavior, not a literature review system. Violates EXC-03 (narrative/empirical piece lacking a described system architecture for literature workflow).

Review article exploring AI applications in rheumatology research (diagnosis, prognosis, drug discovery, clinical trials). Discusses both discriminative and generative AI but does not propose, implement, or evaluate a computational tool for literature review workflow. No system architecture, no provenance mechanisms, no empirical evaluation of a literature harness. Violates EXC-03 (narrative review/commentary lacking computational artifact for literature workflow).

Evaluates probability rating performance of 4 LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4, Phi 4, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen 2.5) for title/abstract screening in systematic literature reviews. Assesses accuracy, consistency between probability and qualitative ratings, and recommends multi-LLM assistance. Directly evaluates LLMs as tools for SLR screening (INC-01), incorporates LLMs (INC-02), provides quantitative empirical evaluation with metrics (INC-04). No exclusion criteria apply.

Title indicates evaluation of LLMs for SLR automation focusing on quality and time savings. No abstract available to verify details, but title strongly suggests empirical evaluation of LLM-based SLR automation tools. Included provisionally based on title alignment with INC-01 (evaluates tool for SLR), INC-02 (LLMs), INC-04 (evaluation of quality/time). Low confidence due to missing abstract; would benefit from full-text review.

Proposes LLM-based ranking approach for screening prioritization in systematic literature reviews for disease model parameter extraction. Uses zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting to frame selection criteria as QA task. Validated across 4 zoonotic disease datasets achieving 70% work effort reduction at 95% recall (NWSS@95%). Provides explainable AI rationales. Matches INC-01 (tool for screening prioritization), INC-02 (LLM), INC-04 (quantitative empirical evaluation across multiple datasets). No exclusion criteria apply.

Framework paper examining LLM applications in healthcare domain. Provides conceptual framework, evolutionary trajectory, prospective avenues, and challenges. Does not propose or implement a computational tool for literature discovery, screening, extraction, or synthesis. No system architecture for literature workflow, no provenance mechanisms, no empirical evaluation of a literature harness. Violates EXC-03 (narrative/framework piece lacking computational artifact for literature workflow). Only weakly matches INC-02 (discusses LLMs).

Commentary/living review update analyzing 117 publications on automated data extraction for clinical systematic reviews, focusing on 17 LLM-based papers. Discusses evaluation strategies, reporting inconsistencies, and potential applications. It is a review of methods, not a computational tool itself. No new system architecture, no provenance mechanisms, no empirical evaluation of a novel harness. Violates EXC-03 (commentary/review lacking computational artifact for literature workflow).

Introduces LLAssist, an open-source tool for automating literature reviews using LLMs and NLP. Extracts important information from articles and evaluates relevance to user-defined research questions. Available on arXiv with DOI. Matches INC-01 (computational tool for literature review automation), INC-02 (LLMs/NLP), INC-04 (accessible codebase implied by open-source designation). No exclusion criteria apply.

Case study evaluating GPT-4o Mini and Claude 3.5 Sonnet for title/abstract screening in a systematic review on precision livestock farming. Assesses screening accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, time, and cost compared to human raters. Demonstrates LLM-assisted screening improves quality with low extra resources. Matches INC-01 (evaluates LLMs as tools for SLR screening), INC-02 (LLMs), INC-04 (quantitative empirical evaluation with accuracy metrics and cost analysis). No exclusion criteria apply.

Comparative study evaluating 8 LLMs for clinical decision support on early maxillary expansion (healthcare domain). Assesses accuracy, comprehensiveness, readability of LLM responses to parental questions. Not a tool for academic literature review or evidence synthesis workflow. Violates EXC-02 (general-purpose clinical LLM evaluation not targeted to scholarly literature). Only weakly matches INC-02 (uses LLMs).

Introduces OpenScholar, a specialized retrieval-augmented LM answering scientific queries by identifying passages from 45M open-access papers with citation-backed responses. Develops ScholarQABench benchmark (2,967 queries, 208 long-form answers). Outperforms GPT-4o by 6.1% in correctness; achieves citation accuracy on par with human experts (vs 78-90% hallucination for GPT-4o). Open-sources code, models, datastore, data, public demo. Matches all inclusion criteria: literature synthesis tool (INC-01), RAG/LLM (INC-02), citation verification/hallucination mitigation (INC-03), benchmark + open-source (INC-04). No exclusion criteria apply.

Living systematic review update of data extraction methods for clinical systematic reviews (117 publications). Reviews and categorizes existing approaches including LLM-based extraction. It is a review of methods, not a computational tool itself. No new system architecture, no provenance mechanisms, no empirical evaluation of a novel harness. Violates EXC-03 (review/commentary lacking computational artifact for literature workflow).

Compares multiple approaches to automate literature review generation: frequency-based (spaCy), transformer (Simple T5), and RAG with GPT-3.5-turbo. Evaluates on SciTLDR dataset using ROUGE scores. Finds GPT-3.5-turbo achieves highest ROUGE-1 (0.364). Creates GUI for best system. Matches INC-01 (implements systems for auto-generating literature reviews), INC-02 (RAG/LLM), INC-04 (quantitative evaluation with ROUGE metrics). No exclusion criteria apply.

Title indicates transformer-based model for citation context extraction using QA task. Citation context extraction is a component of citation graph analysis and literature synthesis workflows. No abstract available to verify architecture, evaluation, or provenance mechanisms. Included provisionally based on title relevance to INC-01 (tool for citation analysis) and INC-02 (transformer/LLM). Low confidence due to missing abstract; requires full-text review to confirm INC-03/INC-04.

Introduces novel multi-AI-agent system for fully automating systematic literature reviews. Leverages LLMs to streamline search string generation, inclusion/exclusion filtering, abstract summarization, and research question analysis. Provides user-friendly interface and GitHub code (https://github.com/GPT-Laboratory/SLR-automation). Empirical evaluation demonstrates substantial time/effort reduction while maintaining comprehensiveness and precision. Matches all inclusion criteria: multi-agent SLR system (INC-01), LLMs/agentic orchestration (INC-02), describes operational framework with filtering/summarization (INC-03), provides codebase and empirical evaluation (INC-04). No exclusion criteria apply.

arXiv preprint version of OpenScholar (same as SCI-000154). Specialized retrieval-augmented LM for scientific literature synthesis with citation-backed responses. Develops ScholarQABench benchmark. Outperforms GPT-4o and PaperQA2 in correctness; achieves human-expert citation accuracy. Open-sources all artifacts. Matches all inclusion criteria identically to SCI-000154. No exclusion criteria apply.

Review of machine learning for analyzing accident reports in construction industry. Organizes literature by data pre-processing, algorithms, testing/implementation, data structure. Identifies limitations in data availability, manual structuring, unsupervised learning use. Proposes standardized development methods for ML safety analysis. It is a domain-specific review of ML applications, not a computational tool for literature review workflow. No system for literature discovery, screening, extraction, or synthesis. Violates EXC-03 (review lacking computational artifact for literature workflow).
